user.title: Set up Fellow Stagg EKG
user.description: Add your kettle by entering its IP address (find it in your router's client list), or scan the local network for kettles.

pick.title: Scan for kettles
pick.description: Choose which network to scan. The field is prefilled with a network Home Assistant is connected to — if your kettle is on a different subnet or an IoT VLAN, enter that network instead (e.g. 192.168.20.0/24, or just an IP on it to scan its /24). Scanning another VLAN only works if your firewall lets Home Assistant reach it over HTTP.

data_description.name: Device name (also the entity-ID prefix). Leave blank to use the kettle's detected model name.

manual.title: Set up Fellow Stagg EKG
manual.description: Enter the IP address of your kettle and select your preferred temperature unit for Home Assistant.

data_description.name: Device name (also the entity-ID prefix). Leave blank to use the kettle's detected model name.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the kettle. Please check the IP address and ensure the kettle is powered on and connected to your network.
error.invalid_network: Enter a network like 192.168.20.0/24 (no larger than /22) or an IP address on it.
error.no_kettles_found: No kettle answered on that network. Check that you scanned the subnet the kettle is on (see your router's client list), or go back and add it by IP address instead.
error.incomplete_response: The kettle answered, but its response could not be fully understood, so setup was stopped (the temperature entities would not work). Make sure the kettle is sitting on its base and try again. If it keeps failing, check the Home Assistant log for the raw response and run examples/probe_kettle.py — your firmware may format responses differently.

data_description.temperature_unit: The unit Home Assistant uses for this kettle's entities, presets and actions. The kettle's own display has a separate setting: the Kettle Display Unit control on the device page.
data_description.temp_set_method: Direct uses firmware set-target commands with verification (fast). Dial emulates the physical dial (slower but works on firmwares without a set-target command).
data_description.poll_interval: How often to read the kettle's state while it's off (5-60 seconds)
data_description.active_poll_interval: How often to read the kettle's state while it's heating or keeping warm (2-60 seconds) — faster polling keeps the temperature and Kettle State fresh
data_description.presets: One-tap heat buttons as 'Name: temperature' pairs separated by commas, in your configured unit — e.g. 'Pour-over: 96, Green tea: 79'. A Boil button is always included.
data_description.sync_clock: When enabled, the kettle's display clock is set to Home Assistant's local time on startup and once a day (handles drift and DST). A manual Sync Clock button is always available.

error.invalid_presets: Presets must be 'Name: temperature' pairs separated by commas, within 40-100 °C (104-212 °F), with unique names — e.g. 'Pour-over: 96, Green tea: 79'.

kettle_unreachable.title: Kettle at {host} is not responding
kettle_unreachable.description:
Home Assistant cannot connect to the kettle at {host} on port 80.

If the kettle still looks connected to WiFi (it answers `ping {host}` and shows in your router's client list) but `curl http://{host}/cli?cmd=state` hangs, the kettle firmware's web server has wedged — a known issue with the kettle's firmware, often after long or back-to-back heating sessions.

**Fix: unplug the kettle's base for about 10 seconds and plug it back in.** Entities recover automatically within ~30 seconds; this issue then clears itself.

If the kettle isn't on WiFi at all, check its power and the Fellow app. While the kettle is unreachable, the integration polls more slowly to avoid stressing it, and keeps retrying indefinitely.

firmware_cli_muted.title: Kettle firmware {version} stopped local control
firmware_cli_muted.description:
The kettle at {host} updated itself to firmware {version}. This firmware no longer returns any output from the local command interface this integration uses, so Home Assistant can't read or control the kettle. Unplugging it doesn't help.

The kettle still has firmware {spare_version} in its spare slot ({spare_slot}), so you can switch back:

1. **Block the kettle's internet access first** with a router rule that keeps local access. Otherwise it reinstalls the update within about 30 minutes.
2. Open `http://{host}/cli?cmd=setpart+{spare_slot}` in a browser.
3. Open `http://{host}/` and check that it shows `Boot partition: {spare_slot}`. If it doesn't, stop here.
4. Open `http://{host}/cli?cmd=reset`. The page won't load while the kettle restarts; that's expected.
5. After about 30 seconds, `http://{host}/` should show `Current version: {spare_version}`. Reload this integration, then turn on **Keep the kettle's clock synced** in its options, since the kettle can no longer get the time from the internet.

Keep the internet block on permanently. Never send `eraseotherpart`: it erases the spare slot, and with it the way back. This issue clears itself once the kettle answers again.

firmware_cli_muted_no_rollback.title: Kettle firmware {version} stopped local control
firmware_cli_muted_no_rollback.description:
The kettle at {host} is running firmware {version}, which no longer returns any output from the local command interface this integration uses, so Home Assistant can't read or control the kettle. Unplugging it doesn't help.

No older firmware was found in the kettle's spare slot, so it can't be switched back the usual way. Block the kettle's internet access to stop further updates, and see the linked instructions for other options, including a Bluetooth-based integration that supports this firmware. This issue clears itself once the kettle answers again.
